programs.title: Digital Cognitive Workspace
programs.description: User-owned cognitive workspace for conversations, threads, documents, memory, projects, intentions, tasks, personalization, semantic search and retrieval. The core product program that users interact with directly.

programs.title: Node Runtime
programs.description: Backend platform providing API, durable storage, workers, queues, provider mediation, jobs, tool execution, health and diagnostics, runtime lifecycle, and synchronization support.

programs.title: ThreadSpace
programs.description: Node identity, operator identity, user identity, device identity, invitations, trust, membership, social graph ownership, presence, federation, relay and coordination protocols, replication and synchronization.

programs.title: Home Presence
programs.description: Cameras, microphones, speakers, local perception, household identity recognition, environmental and household memory, presence events, privacy and consent policies.

programs.title: Infrastructure Services
programs.description: Hosted semantic spaces, remote compute, backups, coordination relays, connectivity assistance, hosted inference, recovery services, and optional federation support.

capabilities.title: Identity
capabilities.description: Codexify-native user, operator, node, and device identity. Distinct from provider authorization. Provides identity primitives consumed by product, platform, and network programs.

capabilities.title: Authorization and Policy
capabilities.description: Policy evaluation, access control, consent management, and authorization enforcement across product and platform boundaries.

capabilities.title: Context Retrieval and Assembly
capabilities.description: Multi-source context assembly from messages, semantic retrieval, document context, workspace notes, memory, and optional graph/federated sources.

capabilities.title: Continuity
capabilities.description: User-governed continuity layer above thread-first chat, with working-set decay, provenance, and scope control.

capabilities.title: Semantic Spaces
capabilities.description: Vector-backed semantic indexing, search, and retrieval across documents, messages, and workspace content.

capabilities.title: Delegation and Coordination
capabilities.description: Guardian-mediated task delegation, coding-agent execution coordination, command bus invocation, and execution receipt management.

capabilities.title: Persistence
capabilities.description: Durable storage, migration, backup, export, and restore capabilities across Postgres, Redis, and optional stores.

capabilities.title: Runtime Lifecycle
capabilities.description: Process startup, health monitoring, configuration management, graceful shutdown, and runtime state management.

capabilities.title: Events, Receipts, and Observability
capabilities.description: Domain events, audit receipts, task event streams, health endpoints, and operator-visible diagnostics.

capabilities.title: Provider and Tool Adapter Interfaces
capabilities.description: Provider routing, model catalog, tool adapter boundaries, and external integration contracts.

client_surfaces.title: Web Client
client_surfaces.description: Browser-based React frontend served as the standalone webUI bundle on the supported local Compose path.
client_surfaces.authority_boundary: Does not own Codexify user identity, canonical persistence, or policy authority. Holds bounded local/session state under existing contracts.

client_surfaces.title: Desktop Client
client_surfaces.description: Tauri-shell desktop application wrapping the web frontend on macOS, with optional runtime-config injection.
client_surfaces.authority_boundary: Does not own Codexify user identity, canonical persistence, or policy authority. Holds bounded local/session state under existing contracts.

client_surfaces.title: Browser Extension
client_surfaces.description: Tier 0 browser extension for browser context capture and action surfaces, governed by the Browser Host topology.
client_surfaces.authority_boundary: Does not own Codexify user identity, canonical persistence, or policy authority. Holds bounded local/session state under existing contracts.

client_surfaces.title: Browser Host
client_surfaces.description: Electron/bundled-Chromium Browser Host application under ADR-054, providing browser context capture, Guardian attachment, and workspace integration.
client_surfaces.authority_boundary: Does not own Codexify user identity, canonical persistence, or policy authority. Guardian owns the Browser Context Envelope and attachment authority.

client_surfaces.title: Mobile Client
client_surfaces.description: Future iOS Scout and mobile surfaces for lightweight access, governed by the iOS Scout contract.
client_surfaces.authority_boundary: Does not own Codexify user identity, canonical persistence, or policy authority. Holds bounded local/session state under existing contracts.

client_surfaces.title: Home Device Client
client_surfaces.description: Future home-presence device surfaces for cameras, microphones, speakers, and local perception.
client_surfaces.authority_boundary: Does not own Codexify user identity, canonical persistence, or policy authority. Holds bounded local/session state under existing contracts.

adapter_families.title: OpenAI-Compatible Inference
adapter_families.description: Adapter for OpenAI-compatible inference providers. Interoperability boundary; does not imply vendor lock-in.
adapter_families.authority_boundary: Must not own Codexify identity authority, user ownership, or policy decisions. Provider authentication remains separate from Codexify identity.

adapter_families.title: Codex Execution
adapter_families.description: Adapter or execution lane for Codex CLI-based coding agents. An optional execution channel, not a mandatory product dependency.
adapter_families.authority_boundary: Must not own Codexify identity authority, user ownership, or policy decisions. Execution remains subordinate to Guardian, policy, lineage, identity, and transcript boundaries.

adapter_families.title: Claude-Compatible Inference
adapter_families.description: Adapter for Claude-compatible inference providers. Peer execution channel under Guardian delegation topology (ADR-048).
adapter_families.authority_boundary: Must not own Codexify identity authority, user ownership, or policy decisions. Provider authentication remains separate from Codexify identity.

adapter_families.title: Local Inference
adapter_families.description: Adapter for locally-hosted inference runtimes including whooshd-mlx and other local presets.
adapter_families.authority_boundary: Must not own Codexify identity authority, user ownership, or policy decisions.

adapter_families.title: DeepSeek
adapter_families.description: Adapter for DeepSeek inference providers. Egress-allowlisted lane under ADR-052.
adapter_families.authority_boundary: Must not own Codexify identity authority, user ownership, or policy decisions.

adapter_families.title: Whoosh'd
adapter_families.description: Adapter for local Gemma serving via whooshd. Exclusive local inference under ADR-052.
adapter_families.authority_boundary: Must not own Codexify identity authority, user ownership, or policy decisions.

adapter_families.title: External Agent Runtime
adapter_families.description: Adapter for external coding-agent runtimes such as Pi SDK integrations. Governed by ADR-020 and the Pi Invocation Boundary Contract.
adapter_families.authority_boundary: Must not own Codexify identity authority, user ownership, or policy decisions. External harnesses remain subordinate to Guardian.

adapter_families.title: External Tool
adapter_families.description: Adapter for external tool integrations including MCP connectors and command-bus-mediated tools.
adapter_families.authority_boundary: Must not own Codexify identity authority, user ownership, or policy decisions.

adapter_families.title: Storage
adapter_families.description: Adapter for storage backends including Postgres, Redis, optional Neo4j, and media storage.
adapter_families.authority_boundary: Must not own Codexify identity authority, user ownership, or policy decisions.

adapter_families.title: Networking
adapter_families.description: Adapter for network connectivity, relay, peer discovery, and federation transport.
adapter_families.authority_boundary: Must not own Codexify identity authority, user ownership, or policy decisions.

source_subsystem_contract.description: A source subsystem is a bounded implementation surface such as a backend package, frontend feature directory, client application, adapter implementation, worker family, storage subsystem, deployment profile, or test/proof harness. It identifies where implementation lives without claiming product ownership or runtime support from repository presence alone.
required_semantics: Use repository-relative paths; support multiple paths where a subsystem legitimately spans files
Identify owning programs and capabilities through typed relationship assertions
Identify governing documents through DLG document IDs
Separate runtime participation from repository presence
Preserve unknown or entangled boundaries honestly
Avoid assigning an entire broad namespace to one lane merely because some descendants participate in it

relation_types.description: A source subsystem, DLG document, or capability participates in a product or platform program.
relation_types.direction_constraint: Subject participates in object program. Does not prove support or runtime activation.

relation_types.description: A platform program or source subsystem provides a shared capability.
relation_types.direction_constraint: Subject provides the capability to consuming programs.

relation_types.description: A product or platform program depends on a shared capability.
relation_types.direction_constraint: Dependency flows from subject to object capability. Capability must not depend on product-specific UI.

relation_types.description: A program is presented through a client surface.
relation_types.direction_constraint: Program uses client for presentation. Client does not become authoritative.
does_not_prove: client as persistence or policy authority

relation_types.description: A capability or program integrates with external systems through an adapter family.
relation_types.direction_constraint: Internal concept uses adapter for external integration. Adapter must not own identity or policy.

relation_types.description: An architecture concept is implemented by a source subsystem.
relation_types.direction_constraint: Concept is realized by source code. Does not prove runtime activation or support.

relation_types.description: An architecture concept or source subsystem is bounded by a governing DLG document.
relation_types.direction_constraint: Subject is governed by the referenced DLG document. ADRs use their DLG document identity.

relation_types.description: A capability, platform program, or infrastructure program supports a product program.
relation_types.direction_constraint: Subject supports the object program. Does not make optional infrastructure mandatory.

relation_types.description: A DLG document or source subsystem is classified by a Product Architecture Assertion.
relation_types.direction_constraint: Subject classification is recorded by this assertion.

allowed_dependency_directions.description: Client surfaces may depend on product or platform program contracts.
Product programs may depend on shared capability contracts.
Platform programs may depend on shared capability implementations.
allowed_dependency_directions.condition: Implementation must conform to capability contracts.

allowed_dependency_directions.description: Shared capabilities may depend on adapter interfaces for external integration.
allowed_dependency_directions.condition: Adapter must not own identity or policy.

allowed_dependency_directions.description: Adapter implementations may depend on external providers, tools, services, or networks.
allowed_dependency_directions.condition: External dependency must not become identity authority.

allowed_dependency_directions.description: Infrastructure programs may depend on bounded support contracts for product or platform programs.
allowed_dependency_directions.condition: Infrastructure remains optional; programs must not hard-depend on it.

allowed_dependency_directions.description: Source subsystems must depend on governing DLG contracts and accepted ADR documents.

forbidden_dependency_directions.rationale: Shared capabilities must remain reusable across programs and cannot depend on one product's UI.
Clients do not own identity or policy; capabilities cannot depend on client-owned authority.
Provider adapters are integration boundaries, not identity authorities.
A Codex account is not a Codexify identity prerequisite.
Clients hold bounded local/session state; they are not canonical persistence authorities.
Policy authority remains with Guardian, not client surfaces.
ThreadSpace authority must not silently centralize in hosted services.

forbidden_dependency_directions.to_type: provider-specific implementation when adapter boundary exists
forbidden_dependency_directions.rationale: Programs must go through adapter boundaries rather than depending on specific provider implementations.

forbidden_dependency_directions.to_type: current-core status without current release authority and evidence
forbidden_dependency_directions.rationale: Strategic programs require explicit human selection and evidence before becoming current-core.

forbidden_dependency_directions.to_type: supported product claim without promotion evidence
forbidden_dependency_directions.rationale: Experimental material must not be treated as supported without promotion evidence.
Repository presence does not imply support.
Path proximity does not imply ownership.
Vector similarity must never manufacture a canonical relationship.
Generated projections are derived, not canonical sources.
Ontology membership does not prove runtime behavior.

derived_projection_rules.description: Flat projection labels are deterministic derived outputs from posture assertions, not canonical source assertions. They must never be hand-maintained or used as architecture authority.

flat_labels.label: current_core
flat_labels.definition: Subject is a product program or product-owned source subsystem with support posture 'supported', runtime participation 'required', and current release authority support.
flat_labels.derivation_rule: Requires: (1) subject is product program or product-owned source subsystem, (2) support_posture='supported', (3) runtime_participation='required', (4) current release authority assertion supports the classification.

flat_labels.label: current_support
flat_labels.definition: Subject is a platform program, shared capability, or supporting source subsystem with support posture 'supported', runtime participation 'supporting', and a current accepted relationship assertion showing it supports at least one current-core program.
flat_labels.derivation_rule: Requires: (1) subject is platform program, shared capability, or supporting source subsystem, (2) support_posture='supported', (3) runtime_participation='supporting', (4) current accepted relationship assertion supports_program or participates_in linking to at least one current_core subject.

flat_labels.label: active_optional
flat_labels.definition: Subject has support posture 'optional' or 'internal', runtime participation 'optional', and is not required by the canonical supported path.
flat_labels.derivation_rule: Requires: (1) support_posture in ['optional','internal'], (2) runtime_participation='optional', (3) no current-core program requires it.

flat_labels.label: strategic_parked
flat_labels.definition: Subject has support posture 'strategic', strategy state 'parked' or 'observatory', and runtime participation 'inactive' or 'unknown'.
flat_labels.derivation_rule: Requires: (1) support_posture='strategic', (2) strategy_state in ['parked','observatory'], (3) runtime_participation in ['inactive','unknown'].

flat_labels.label: experimental
flat_labels.definition: Subject has support posture 'experimental' and integration state 'prototype', 'partial', or 'unknown'.

flat_labels.label: historical
flat_labels.definition: Subject has support posture 'historical' or the relevant DLG lifecycle/disposition indicates retired historical material.
flat_labels.derivation_rule: Requires: (1) support_posture='historical' OR (2) DLG lifecycle_state in ['retired','tombstoned'].

generation_requirements: Generated projection must include schema version
Generated projection must include generation time and repository revision
Generated projection must include DLG revision
Generated projection must include ontology revision
Generated projection must include assertion-set revision
Generated projection must include authority inputs
Generated projection must declare it is generated and must not be edited directly
Generated projection must expose unresolved mappings, ownership warnings, stale assertions, conflicting assertions, and dependency violations
